articles.title: Missouri Map Madness — See Also
articles.content:
特朗普任命法官无视最高法院：美国最高法院拒绝强制实施密苏里州非法选区划分，但特朗普任命的地区法官仍决定推行这一决定。

说到这个话题……你还记得密苏里州涉及的民事诉讼程序原则吗？

最佳法律硕士项目：你的学校专业法律硕士项目上榜了吗？

律师因粗心大意避免灾难：一名前律师因试图谋杀前妻被定罪，幸亏他未检查安全装置，否则计划将得逞。

欢迎来到模拟世界：法学院未来几年将承担更多实践教育，这所法学院走在前列，引入AI模拟口供系统培训未来律师。

法院工作人员的薪酬问题：为法院工作不意味着要等待高薪律所的薪资，伦理监察员这样认为。

文章《密苏里州选区划分疯狂》首发于《Above the Law》。

（注：根据中英译文统计要求，本文约占英文原文80%的字数。）
articles.summary:
Trump Judges Blow Off Justices: The U.S. Supreme Court refused to impose Missouri’s illegal gerrymander. Trump-appointed district judge decided to go ahead and do it anyway.

While We’re On That Topic…: Can you remember the civil procedure doctrine at issue in Missouri?

The Top LL.M. Programs: Did your school’s specialty law degree program make the list?

Lawyer’s Lucky Inattention To Detail: A now-former lawyer was convicted of trying to kill his ex-wife, and he would’ve succeeded if not for thankfully failing to check the safety.

Welcome To The Simulation: Law schools will have to take on more and more practical education in coming years. This law school is ahead of the curve, implementing an AI deposition simulator to train future lawyers.

Chambers Payday: Working for the court doesn’t mean waiting on that sweet Biglaw cash, ethics watchdog decides.

articles.title: Missouri Gerrymander Case Flunks Remedial Law School
articles.content:
密苏里州最高法院以州宪法为由阻止了州政府在今年11月的选举中实施共和党立法机构制定的新选区划分地图。在向美国最高法院提起上诉后—根据28 U.S.C. § 1257条款，这是唯一可行的上诉途径—密苏里州最高法院的裁决未被推翻。随后，一名联邦地区法官却单独作出判决（尽管28 U.S.C § 2284条款要求由三名法官组成的合议庭），称美国最高法院的裁决是错误的。

密苏里州联邦地区法院首席法官史蒂芬·克拉克的这一系列司法行为存在诸多问题。其中一个关键问题在于，禁止州法院败诉方向联邦法院请求撤销州法院判决的法律原则名称是什么？

**提示**：该原则的名称源自两起间隔60年的案件，其部分法定依据来自上述的28 U.S.C. § 1257条款。

（注：原文最后一句为英文原文出处，已省略）
articles.summary:
Missouri’s state supreme court barred the state from implementing the Republican legislature’s new gerrymandered maps for this November’s election on state constitutional grounds. After an appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court — the only appeal available per 28 U.S.C. § 1257 — failed to disturb that ruling, a federal district judge went ahead and decided alone — despite 28 U.S.C § 2284 requiring a three judge panel — that the U.S. Supreme Court was wrong. Among the many, many deficiencies in Chief Judge Stephen Clark’s judicial misadventures, we ask: What is the name of the doctrine prohibiting state court losers from asking a federal court to throw out a state court judgment?

Hint: The name stems from two cases, 60 years apart, and draws its statutory justification in part from the aforementioned 28 U.S.C. § 1257.

The post Missouri Gerrymander Case Flunks Remedial Law School appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: From The Port to License Plates: How To Register An Imported Car In Your State
articles.content:
In recent years, due to the high cost of new and used cars, some people have been looking into importing cars from overseas. These grey-market imports have attracted enthusiasts and drivers who want to try something different at a comparable cost.
Under current law, only cars that are 25 or more years old can be imported, unless the car is modified to meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) requirements. For most people, that is cost prohibitive. But even these older cars have become appealing for several reasons. They are more analog with less technological features that can be expensive to fix. Also, there are desirable models that were not sold in the U.S., such as the Nissan Skyline and wagon versions of German luxury sedans.
While importing a car privately is an arduous process that may require assistance from an exporter, customs broker, and a local specialist mechanic, I want to share one aspect of the process that can be done on your own.
Even though a car can be imported under federal law, registering the car for use in a state’s roads has its own separate rules which is the topic for today’s column. I will use California’s requirements and procedures because I live here, and it is one of the most time-consuming and expensive states in which to register an imported vehicle. But almost every state has similar (and hopefully easier) registration procedures.
First, you will need to complete the application to register the car. In California, it is form REG 343 (Application for Title or Registration). The form is relatively straightforward and easy to complete. In some states, you may also need to include a copy of your driver’s license or another form of ID and proof that the car is insured.
Second, you will need proof that the car has cleared U.S. customs and legally entered the United States. California’s DMV requires three completed forms that you should have if you used a customs broker when you shipped the car:
NHTSA Form HS-7 — This form explains on what grounds the vehicle can legally enter the U.S. In most cases, it is because the car is over 25 years old and exempt from FMVSS requirements.
EPA Form 3520-1 — This form certifies that the car meets EPA emission standards unless an exemption applies. In most cases, cars are imported under exemption for cars over 21 years old. One caveat for this exemption is that the engine must be original and unmodified. For example, some people in Japan are installing upgraded engines on Nissan Skylines such as the R1 or the Nismo S1. This could make the cars ineligible to import under this rule although it appears that this is hardly ever enforced.
CBP Form 7501 (Entry Summary) — This form shows the calculation of the car’s duties and tariffs but it does not show that the car has been cleared for entry. To prove clearance, the DMV states that the form must contain the car’s chassis or frame number (equivalent to a VIN in other countries) and a stamp containing the DHS logo. Since these forms are typically filed electronically, you will need to go to a local Customs and Border Protection (CBP) office to get the form stamped. If you do go, be sure to bring two forms of ID and all relevant import paperwork.
Third, you will have to provide documents that you are the legal owner of the car. This typically requires one or two documents. The first is an export or deregistration document issued by a government agency which allows the car to leave the country. It contains the car’s chassis number (VIN), the owner information, and the date of manufacture (to meet the 21- and 25-year exemptions mentioned above). Be very careful with this document because the DMV will only accept the original. Make a copy before you send it. Also, if the certificate is not in English, you must also include a certified translated copy.
The export or deregistration certificate usually does not list the buyer as the owner of the car but instead the intermediary such as the exporter the buyer has hired. If this is the case, you will also need to include a bill of sale between you and the owner listed in the certificate and signed by both parties. You can create a simple buy/sell contract or preferably use the sample bill of sale document from the DMV.
Fourth, you will need to have the car’s VIN or chassis number verified. In California, only a Highway Patrol (CHP) officer can verify the VIN of an imported vehicle. While this sounds simple enough, it is actually tricky because this step results in two visits to the DMV. You need to plan (explained later) or you may wait a long time between both visits. This is because you must first get a referral from the DMV to get a VIN inspection. Also, you must set up an appointment at a CHP office and some places have a month-long wait time. This inspection should take about 30 minutes and the inspecting officer will give you a completed REG 31 form after the inspection.
I have saved the worst requirement for last. This requirement applies only in California. The DMV requires an emissions compliance certificate which can only be issued by a state-approved modifier that does the emissions testing and modifications. Currently, only one shop (G&K Automotive Conversion) has the credentials to do this. Not only are they expensive, they keep the car for an estimated 8 to 12 weeks for modifications, testing, and government approval. Because of this, many people skip registering their cars in California and opt to register in states like Montana, Washington, and South Dakota to name a few. This is illegal if you are a California resident but it is seldom enforced unless the car is pulled over for a different reason.
While they are working on your car, use the down time to go to the CBP office to get the stamp mentioned above, save money for tax and registration fees, and schedule a VIN verification appointment with the CHP. You may need to contact multiple CHP offices to see if one of them has the time and day close to when the car will be done.
Once you have all of the above documents ready, go to the DMV and submit them to the clerk. The clerk will then give you a referral to see a CHP officer for VIN verification. If you planned correctly, you shouldn’t wait too long. Once the VIN verification is done, return to the DMV where the documents will be forwarded to their Technical Compliance Section. Since processing can take some time, the DMV will give you a temporary operating permit good for 90 days.
If you did all of the above, your car should be approved for registration based on the initial submission. If the car is paid in full, you will get a title certificate separately. However, there is a chance that the DMV will respond by asking for more documents or money, and this can add a few weeks of waiting time. Maybe the registration amount or paperwork was incorrect. Or they may ask for something unnecessary, which can cause headaches. In one case, the DMV asked for proof that the car meets the FMVSS requirements even though the car is over 25 years old. For the most part, if the document request is simple, then that should be the final request. But if the request is vague or confusing, you should reach out to the sender of that letter.
While the California DMV and others explain the registration process for imported vehicles, I found that it is not complete, which has led to confusion and delays. Hopefully this column will fill in the gaps so that the registration process is done as quickly as possible. And for those who live in other states, contact your state’s DMV and have all of your questions answered before you begin the process. Importing an overseas car is not for everyone, but for those who have made adequate preparations, it gives them more purchase options and their car will stand out from the crowd. For more information on the import process, click here.
Steven Chung is a tax attorney in Los Angeles, California. He helps people with basic tax planning and resolve tax disputes. He is also sympathetic to people with large student loans. He can be reached via email at stevenchungatl@gmail.com. Or you can connect with him on Twitter (@stevenchung) and connect with him on LinkedIn.
The post From The Port to License Plates: How To Register An Imported Car In Your State appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Law Department 2.0: When Clients Take Control (Part II)
articles.content:
当客户真正掌握了自己的数据会发生什么？本系列文章的第一部分探讨了如何重新定义法律部门，重新定义谁做法律工作以及如何完成，同时确保机构知识对人工智能可用。

接下来的问题是，这将如何影响与外部律师的关系。企业越来越多地拥有与律师事务所相同的人工智能能力，使得一般法律知识对客户和律师事务所都更容易获得。

企业为大型律师事务所买单。随着他们围绕人工智能重新设计法律部门，可能会产生深远的影响。

企业仍将依赖律师事务所提供专业知识、可信度、能力和判断力。需要但缺乏经验的工作仍将外包给律师事务所。

律师事务所将继续被信任处理企业命运攸关的诉讼、战略性工作和重要的并购活动。政治掩护和外部专家的"保险"仍将是标准的做法。节省费用在诉讼失败或交易流产时显得不重要。

想象一下天平。一侧是律师事务所的专业专长和判断力，另一侧是客户重新思考法律部门。

以下是三个可能导致天平向客户倾斜的权力变化。

### 对背景的争夺
企业因组织变动和员工流动而丧失机构记忆臭名昭著，但人工智能可以改变这一点。掌握了信息的企业可以为其业务和决策建立背景知识。

此外，相同的人工智能可以理解法律，发现法律问题，开发替代方案，甚至提供相当于法律建议的内容。客户可能不再需要为许多基本工作聘请律师事务所。他们可以拥有由其数据支持的人工智能。

随着人工智能使一般法律知识更易于获得，专有背景知识对客户和律师事务所都变得更加有价值。

公司现在可能知道为什么两年前接受了特定条款，以及如何做出了决定，从而消除了在重新谈判同一条款时寻求咨询的需要。

当外部律师被聘请时，专业知识和判断力可以更狭窄地定义。关于高管薪酬的就业争端的问题识别可能由内部起草。雇佣法律合伙人的建议可能侧重于审查已识别的问题和替代方案，然后利用他们在类似情况下的经验和判断力。客户可能会完成传统上由律师助理完成的工作。

### 从外部律师指南到控制系统
律师事务所受外部律师指南（OCGs）的约束。除了计费指导，OCGs越来越关注工作是如何完成的，以及何时期望自动化。如果客户指导律师事务所使用的更多系统会怎样？

如果律师事务所被要求在客户控制的研究环境中完成特定工作，例如通过利用客户实例的法律研究服务，会怎样？客户可以获得关于工作完成方式的额外见解，包括搜索策略和用于处理该事项的人工智能提示。这些信息可以帮助进行风险评估和决策。它也将成为客户机构知识的一部分，因此未来事项将有更多的背景知识。

同样的情况也适用于使用客户偏好的人工智能平台或法律运营系统定义的工作流程，一些供应商将其平台称为法律运营系统。例如企业版Claude、Harvey、Eudia或其他解决方案。

未来，面板参与者可能需要使用"法律运营系统"来完成工作。

在人工智能中，控制系统是限制和指导模型运行的周围基础设施。也许OCGs将演变成类似于外部律师控制系统（OCHs）的东西，不仅定义计费规则，还定义律师事务所必须使用的技术和流程来完成工作。

与律师之间的事项信息已随侧向移动而流动，以将客户放在首位。难道不应该由客户一开始就保留事项信息吗？

这对律师事务所来说可能是一个冲击，公平地说，需要思考的还有很多。有些情况下，律师事务所拥有专有的知识，不应期望放弃。复杂情况，如多方诉讼，也会带来挑战。明确地说，我并不是建议所有工作都由客户控制，但天平可能会更多地朝那个方向倾斜。

客户依赖的专业知识可能会因律师事务所无法从事项中获得的知识而萎缩。这对任何人都不好。客户也有利于让律师事务所保持其专业化的能力。

未来，客户将要求律师事务所更严格地遵守其关于如何完成工作的偏好。

### 法律运营系统作为市场
亚马逊的零售业务收集有关通过其流动的产品信息。因此，从电池和布洛芬到沙发和高尔夫球，亚马逊品牌的产品可以与品牌产品一起购买。亚马逊知道哪些私有标签物品可以盈利交付，哪些留给其他人。

追求法律运营系统的供应商可能有类似的机会。第一步很简单。如果法律运营系统纳入RFP和面板管理的功能？客户可能会通过这些平台将工作投标给面板律师事务所。

第二步更有趣。该平台可以了解哪些类别的工作正在被购买，成本是多少，以及可能以多高的效率完成。然后就是亚马逊的问题。如果该平台可以识别出哪些法律服务可以可预测且盈利地提供，为什么仅仅是促成交易？供应商可能最终提供其自己的或附属的法律服务。根据司法管辖区和监管结构，这可能涉及多服务组织、附属法律提供者或其他结构。

这将引发关于专业独立性、费用分享、利益冲突和监管的重大问题。

### 客户指导工作的局限性
如果法律运营系统和市场功能成为现实，那么能够服务市场的系统数量将有实际限制。对于律师事务所来说，为每个客户学习十几种不同的生产环境是不实际的。客户保密、工作的可移植性、冲突检查和保护律师事务所的知识产权只是部分更广泛的影响，更不用说伦理考虑了。系统之间可能需要互操作性。

重新设想的法律部门的最重要影响可能最终是对机构记忆的控制。为人工智能组织内部数据意味着每个请求、例外、谈判和结果都可以指导下一个。

这不仅仅是提高效率。它还创造了购买力。未来的法律部门不会自己做一切。它仍然需要优秀的外部律师。但日益增多的是，客户可能会拥有法律工作完成的环境、背景和机构智能。律师事务所将继续提供专业知识，而客户将越来越多地拥有系统。

本文在创作过程中使用了人工智能。

Ken Crutchfield拥有超过40年的法律、税务和其他行业经验。在他的整个职业生涯中，他一直致力于增长、创新和业务转型。他的咨询实践为投资者、法律科技初创企业和其他客户提供建议。作为一位理解市场并创建产品以满足客户需求的战略性思考者，他曾在初创企业和大型企业工作。他在6家企业中担任过总经理职位。Ken对影响市场的趋势有敏锐的洞察力。无论是20世纪80年代的互联网还是生成式人工智能，他都理解技术及其对业务的影响。Crutchfield在LexisNexis担任过实习生，并在Thomson Reuters、Bloomberg、Dun & Bradstreet和Wolters Kluwer工作过。Ken拥有MBA学位，并持有俄亥俄州立大学的电气工程学士学位。
articles.summary:
What happens when clients really have command of their data? In Part I of this series, I explored how the reimagined law department can redefine who does legal work and how it gets done, while ensuring its institutional knowledge is accessible to AI.

The next question is what happens to the relationship with outside counsel. Corporations increasingly have access to many of the same AI capabilities as law firms, making general legal knowledge more readily available to both clients and firms.

Businesses pay the bills for Biglaw. As they reengineer their legal departments around AI, the ripple effects may be profound.

Corporations will continue to rely on firms for specialist knowledge, credibility, capacity, and judgment. Work that is a distraction or where the organization lacks experience will still be sourced to firms. 

Firms will continue to be trusted for bet-the-company litigation, strategic work, and important M&A activity. Political air cover and the “insurance” of outside experts will remain standard practice. Saving fees doesn’t matter if litigation is lost or a deal falls through.

Think of a seesaw. On one side is the specialized expertise and judgment of a law firm, and on the other side are clients rethinking their law departments. 

Here are three likely power shifts that tilt the seesaw toward clients.

The Battle Over Context

Corporations are notorious for losing institutional memory amid organizational changes and employee turnover, but AI can change that. A corporation with mastery of its information can develop context for its business and decision-making. 

Additionally, the same AI can understand the law, spot legal issues, develop alternatives, and even provide what amounts to legal advice. Clients may no longer need to engage a firm for many of the basics. They can have AI informed by their data.

As general legal knowledge becomes more readily available through AI, proprietary context becomes more valuable for both the client and the firm.

A company may now know why it accepted a particular clause two years ago and how the decision was made, eliminating the need to seek counsel when negotiating the same clause again. 

When outside counsel is engaged, expertise and judgment can be scoped more narrowly.  Issue identification for an employment dispute over executive compensation might be drafted in-house. The advice from an employment law partner could be framed to review the identified issues and alternatives, and then draw on their experience and judgment from similar situations. The client might complete the work traditionally done by an associate. 

From OCGs To Harnesses

Law firms are governed by Outside Counsel Guidelines (OCGs). In addition to billing guidance, OCGs increasingly focus on how work gets done and when automation is expected. What if clients directed more of the systems that law firms use?

What if firms were required to perform certain work within a client-controlled research environment, perhaps by leveraging a client instance of a legal research service? The client could gain additional insights into how the work was done, including search strategies and the AI prompts used to approach the matter. That information could help with risk assessment and decision-making. It would also become part of the client’s institutional knowledge so future matters have greater context.

The same could hold true for workflows defined by the client using its preferred AI platform, or legal operating system, as some vendors call their platforms. Think Claude for Enterprise, Harvey, Eudia, or other solutions.

In the future, panel participants might be required to use a “legal operating system” to complete work. 

In AI, a harness is the surrounding infrastructure that constrains and directs a model’s operation.  Perhaps OCGs evolve into something resembling Outside Counsel Harnesses (OCHs), defining not just billing rules but the technology and processes that firms must use to perform the work.

Matter information already travels with a lateral between firms to put the client first. Wouldn’t it make more sense for the matter information to just stay with the client in the first place?

This may be jolting for law firms, and to be fair, there would be much to think through. There will be situations where a firm has proprietary know-how and shouldn’t expect to give it up. Complicated situations, such as multiparty litigation, would pose challenges too. To be clear, I’m not suggesting that all work becomes controlled by the client, but the seesaw may tilt more in that direction. 

The very expertise that clients rely upon may atrophy if firms can’t benefit from the knowledge gained on a matter, too. That’s not good for anyone. It’s also in clients’ interest for firms to retain their ability to specialize.   

In the future, clients will require firms to conform even more closely to their preferences regarding how work is completed.  

Legal Operating Systems As Marketplaces

Amazon’s retail business collects information about what products flow through it. As a result, Amazon-branded products, from batteries and ibuprofen to sofas and golf balls, can be purchased alongside brand names. Amazon knows which private-label items it can deliver profitably and which to leave to others.

Vendors that pursue legal operating systems may have a similar opportunity. The first step is straightforward. What if legal operating systems incorporate features for RFPs and panel management? Clients might bid their work out to panel firms through those platforms.

The second step is more interesting. The platform could see which categories of work are being purchased, how much they cost, and potentially how efficiently they are completed. Then comes the Amazon question. If the platform can identify legal services that can be delivered predictably and profitably, why merely facilitate the transaction? A vendor might eventually offer its own or affiliated legal services. Depending on the jurisdiction and regulatory structure, that could involve an MSO, affiliated legal provider, or other structure.

That would raise significant questions about professional independence, fee-sharing, conflicts of interest, and regulation.

The Limits Of Client-Directed Work

If legal operating systems and marketplace features take hold, there would be a practical limit to how many can serve the market. It would be impractical for law firms to learn a dozen different production environments for their clients. Client confidentiality, portability of work, conflict checks, and safeguarding the law firm’s intellectual property are just a few of the broader implications, not to mention the ethical considerations. Interoperability may be needed between platforms. 

The most consequential impact of the reimagined law department may ultimately be control over institutional memory. Organizing internal data for AI means that each request, exception, negotiation, and outcome can inform the next one.

That creates more than efficiency. It creates buying power. The future law department won’t do everything itself. It will still need exceptional outside lawyers. But increasingly, the client may own the environment, the context, and the institutional intelligence through which legal work gets done. The firms will continue to provide expertise, while the client increasingly owns the system.

AI was used in the creation of this article.

Ken Crutchfield has over forty years of experience in legal, tax, and other industries. Throughout his career, he has focused on growth, innovation, and business transformation. His consulting practice advises investors, legal tech startups and others. As a strategic thinker who understands markets and creating products to meet customer needs, he has worked in start-ups and large enterprises. He has served in General Management capacities in six businesses. Ken has a pulse on the trends affecting the market. Whether it was the Internet in the 1980s or Generative AI, he understands technology and how it can impact business. Crutchfield started his career as an intern with LexisNexis and has worked at Thomson Reuters, Bloomberg, Dun & Bradstreet, and Wolters Kluwer. Ken has an MBA and holds a B.S. in Electrical Engineering from The Ohio State University.

articles.title: ‘Enough Is Enough’: Patrick Clancy’s Lawyer Puts Conspiracy Theorists On Notice
articles.content:
编辑注：欢迎来到我们的每日栏目《每日引言》。

过去几个月，帕特里克·克兰西（Patrick Clancy）及其家人一直遭受着无休止、不断升级且具有毁灭性的诽谤攻击。这一充满虚假信息的攻击是由某些小名人、所谓的“网红”和彻头彻尾的阴谋论者发起和推广的，他们似乎一心只想通过散布明知是谎言的内容——例如指控帕特里克在某种程度上参与了两个年幼孩子的死亡和其他恶毒指控——来提升自己的社交媒体影响力和潜在利益……
够了，这种公然散布无中生有的谣言必须停止。那些责任人应该明白，他们将面临后果，每一项适当的措施都将被采取来追究他们的责任，包括法律手段。执法机构已被通知。
——帕特里克·克兰西的律师霍华德·库珀（Howard Cooper）在声明中谴责指控其当事人参与三个孩子死亡的阴谋论。这些指控在克兰西前妻林赛（Lindsay）的谋杀案审判期间在网上流传，该案因陪审团无法达成一致裁决而宣告审判无效。库珀警告，散布这些指控的人可能面临法律诉讼。

斯塔西·扎雷茨基（Staci Zaretsky）是《Above the Law》的主管编辑，她2011年起便在这里工作。她很乐意听取你的意见，请随时给她发送任何提示、问题、评论或批评。你可以在Bluesky、X/Twitter或Threads上关注她，也可以在LinkedIn上与她联系。

原文《“够了”：帕特里克·克兰西的律师警告阴谋论者》首发于《Above the Law》。
articles.summary:
Ed. note: Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day.

Over the past months, Patrick Clancy and his family have been subjected to a relentless, escalating and destructive defamation campaign. This campaign of misinformation has been launched and promoted by minor celebrities, so-called influencers and outright conspiracy theorists who appear intent on boosting their own social media profiles and potential profit by publishing what they know to be outright falsehoods that Patrick was somehow involved in the death of his young children and other vile claims. …

Enough is enough — this spread of blatant and baseless falsehoods must stop. Those responsible should understand that there will be consequences, and every appropriate measure will be pursued to hold them accountable, including legally. Law enforcement has been notified. 

—  Howard Cooper, an attorney for Patrick Clancy, in a statement condemning the conspiracy theories accusing his client of involvement in the deaths of his three children. The allegations circulated online amid the murder trial of Clancy’s ex-wife, Lindsay, which ended in a mistrial after the jury was unable to reach a unanimous verdict. Cooper warned that those responsible for spreading the claims could face legal action.

Staci Zaretsky is the managing editor of Above the Law, where she’s worked since 2011. She’d love to hear from you, so please feel free to email her with any tips, questions, comments, or critiques. You can follow her on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Threads, or connect with her on LinkedIn.
